title: Case study: news feed
summary: Fan-out on write vs read, celebrity problem, bounded timeline caches, cursor feeds, ranking and consistency, with a hybrid fan-out lab.

units.title: Guided design: requirements, estimation, API, data model, high-level design
Deep dives: fan-out strategy, timeline cache, ranking and consistency, the lab

labs.title: Hybrid fan-out timeline service: bounded timelines, celebrity merge on read, cursor paging, idempotent posts

outcomes.text: Scope a news-feed prompt in six minutes: ask the clarifying questions that change the design (follow graph shape, feed ordering, consistency of own posts, media), state NFRs as numbers and an explicit out-of-scope list.

Estimate post and feed-read QPS, fan-out write amplification, timeline-cache memory, post storage with replication and feed egress, and tie each number to the decision it drives (partition, cache, async fan-out, hybrid).

Design the feed API (idempotent post creation, cursor-paginated feed, follow/unfollow) and a data model whose partition keys follow the access patterns (posts by author, timelines by reader, graph in both directions).

Draw the post path (API → posts store + outbox/log → fan-out workers → timeline caches) and the read path (timeline cache → hydrate → merge celebrities), justify every box with a requirement or a number, and walk one request through each.
Choose between fan-out on write, fan-out on read and the hybrid with a celebrity threshold, using numbers for a 50 M-follower account, and state when the answer flips.
Design the timeline cache: bounded per-user lists, memory sizing, inactive-user eviction, rebuild on miss, hot-key and stampede protection, and the fallback when a reader scrolls past the window.
Reason about feed consistency: read-your-own-posts, out-of-order fan-out, dedupe across sources, propagation of deletes and unfollows, and what eventual means for a feed.

Implement a hybrid fan-out timeline service in Go that passes its tests under -race: bounded timelines, celebrity merge on read, cursor paging without duplicates or skips, idempotent posts, lazy deletes, eager unfollows.
Explain how a ranked feed changes the architecture (candidate generation, feature hydration, scoring, re-ranking) and what it costs in latency, freshness and storage.
